implementation.name: original-v2-gpudirect-data-path
implementation.scope: The sending-node layout and paths from the original diagram. Compare two separate sends of the same symbolic n-byte payload; no time or throughput scale.
implementation.question: Which copies disappear with GPUDirect RDMA?

purpose: Which copies disappear with GPUDirect RDMA?
storyboard: The GPU owns payload G. The registered host buffer is empty; nothing has crossed the network.
G is copied through the PCIe switch and CPU root complex into host memory. The original GPU payload remains.
The NIC reads the host copy through the root complex and PCIe switch. The host buffer has incurred one n-byte write and one n-byte read.
The NIC sends G to the fabric. This path used host staging; transmission still consumes the network.
Reset the comparison to a new independent send. G remains in GPU memory, and the host buffer stays empty.
The NIC reads G directly from GPU memory over the PCIe peer path. Payload bytes still cross this link; only the host bounce is removed.
The NIC sends the same G to the fabric. Host payload traffic is absent, but PCIe and network transfer remain.
guard: Host payload traffic disappears only in the direct case. NIC access is still a transfer over PCIe, followed by network transmission; no claim of zero transfer, one DMA transaction, or measured speedup.
